recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. No core FHIR change is needed for FHIR-5549; future machine-readable expansion case-sensitivity metadata should be handled through the valueset-caseSensitive extension or terminology-server behavior rather than by adding a ValueSet compose/expansion element.
issue_request: FHIR-5549 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 ValueSet issue asking that caseSensitive either be represented consistently on compose/expansion or removed from define. The accepted resolution was to leave the model unchanged and document that expansions are treated as case sensitive until the defining code system is consulted.
initial_application: The issue was directly applied in SVN-imported git commit 4ccdb66276a122d32d4eefaf7ca2d5c0caf7f030, '#5549 - note about case sensitivity on expansions', from SVN revision 5883. Later edits corrected wording and reorganized nearby ValueSet prose, but preserved the rule.
additional_context: ValueSet is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, so source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml is current build-scoped resource narrative. Later applied issue FHIR-40719 clarified the external valueset-caseSensitive extension in the FHIR Extension Pack so it must reflect the underlying CodeSystem and must not be used when case sensitivity is unknown; that aligns with the core guidance and does not require a core edit.
reconciliation: No source changes were made. The current source already says expansion codes should be treated as case sensitive, implementers should use the correct case, and implementers can consult the underlying code systems to determine whether the defining code system is case sensitive.

related_jiras.note: Later extension-specific clarification for valueset-caseSensitive confirms extension assertions depend on the underlying CodeSystem and does not conflict with the FHIR-5549 core guidance.
Separate DSTU1 expansion manifest issue appeared in searches, but was not needed to decide FHIR-5549 because the accepted documentation change remains present.
